hints: A modulus graph reflects any part of the line $y=2x-3$ that lies below the $x$-axis.
Find the zero of $2x-3$ to locate the vertex, and calculate the value at $x=0$ for the vertical intercept.
Draw two straight rays meeting at the vertex, extending the sketch into negative $x$.
walkthrough:
Find the vertex of the graph by setting the expression inside the modulus to zero:
$$2x - 3 = 0 \implies 2x = 3 \implies x = \dfrac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{At } x = \dfrac{3}{2}: \quad y = \left|2\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) - 3\right| = |3 - 3| = 0$$
$$\text{Vertex coordinates: } \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 0\right)$$

Find the vertical $y$-intercept by evaluating $y$ at $x = 0$:
$$y = |2(0) - 3| = |0 - 3| = |-3| = 3$$
$$\text{Intercept coordinates: } (0, 3)$$

Determine the two linear branches forming the V-shape:
$$\text{For } x \geqslant \dfrac{3}{2}: \quad y = 2x - 3 \quad (\text{straight line with gradient } +2)$$
$$\text{For } x < \dfrac{3}{2}: \quad y = -(2x - 3) = -2x + 3 \quad (\text{straight line with gradient } -2)$$
$$\text{The graph is a symmetrical V-shape with vertex at } \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 0\right) \text{ and } y\text{-intercept at } (0, 3), \text{ extending for negative } x.$$

hints: Use the official question expression $3x-1<|2x-3|$: split the modulus at $x=3/2$.
For $x<3/2$, solve $3x-1<3-2x$; for $x\ge3/2$, solve $3x-1<2x-3$ and retain only values valid on that branch.
Combine the valid branch results and keep the boundary open because the inequality is strict.
walkthrough:
Compare the linear function $y = 3x - 1$ with the modulus function $y = |2x - 3|$ by finding the critical boundary point on the decreasing branch $x < \dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$3x - 1 = -(2x - 3)$$
$$3x - 1 = 3 - 2x$$
$$3x + 2x = 3 + 1$$
$$5x = 4 \implies x = \dfrac{4}{5}$$

Check for an intersection with the increasing branch $x \geqslant \dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$3x - 1 = 2x - 3 \implies 3x - 2x = -3 + 1 \implies x = -2$$
$$\text{Since } -2 < \dfrac{3}{2}, \text{ the value } x = -2 \text{ is not on the branch } x \geqslant \dfrac{3}{2} \text{ and is extraneous.}$$

Alternatively, solve by squaring under the condition $3x - 1 > 0$:
$$(3x - 1)^2 < (2x - 3)^2$$
$$9x^2 - 6x + 1 < 4x^2 - 12x + 9$$
$$5x^2 + 6x - 8 < 0$$
$$(5x - 4)(x + 2) < 0$$
$$\text{Since } 3x - 1 < 0 \leqslant |2x - 3| \text{ is always satisfied for all } x \leqslant \dfrac{1}{3}, \text{ the lower bound } x = -2 \text{ does not restrict the solution.}$$

State the final solution set for the inequality:
$$x < \dfrac{4}{5}$$
